correctness.rationale: Every noncrossing perfect matching of 2n vertices in strictly convex cyclic order has only opposite-parity chords, yielding an n×n permutation incidence matrix X. For any four alternating-parity polygon vertices, pairing the intervening even-length boundary arcs gives two concrete noncrossing completions whose incidence difference is a signed 2×2 checkerboard. For fixed even rows i<k, allowable column pairs join I={i,…,k-1} to its nonempty complement; the complete bipartite column graph is connected, so telescoping generates every row-pair checkerboard integrally. In particular the standard (n-1)^2 basis of the zero-row/zero-column integer lattice is generated: no torsion index or modular rank loss. The covariance quadratic form is the variance of a linear functional and, for strictly positive weights, vanishes iff the functional is constant across the entire matching set. Its orthogonal complement is precisely arrays u_i+v_j, rank (n-1)^2; Walsh's factor -2 preserves this nullspace. Fixing one edge cuts the polygon into two independent Catalan regions; two disjoint noncrossing edges cut three and yield the displayed Catalan product formula. Independent full enumeration of noncrossing matchings for n=2,3,4,5,6 recovered Catalan counts 2,5,14,42,132 and corresponding exact anchored incidence rank 1,4,9,16,25, with exact single-edge Catalan occurrence counts.
